business_scope.primary_industry_name: Direct Online Retail of Portable Battery Generators and Solar Panels

Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus)

Samoa-New Zealand Tax Information Exchange Agreement (not a comprehensive DTAA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2000 (as amended); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2000; International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018); Companies Act 2001; and all applicable regulations and directives issued by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport of each UBO, director, and shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the applicant's country of nationality and notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or recent bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or issuing bank and notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter confirming satisfactory account conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution and notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency, and register of directors/UBOs where a corporate shareholder or corporate UBO exists
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the entity's domicile and notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The licensed registered agent must screen all applicants, directors, shareholders, UBOs, and beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and Samoa's domestic sanctions and counter-terrorism lists. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are classified as higher risk and require senior management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and ongoing enhanced monitoring. Risk-based enhanced due diligence applies where the state of residence, business model, or transaction profile so indicates. All screening records must be retained for at least five years under the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2000.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Companies Office - International Companies Name Reservation and Registration Portal (applications submitted through licensed registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All official filing documents and the registered legal name must be submitted in English using Latin script. A non-Roman script name, including Chinese, may be adopted as a secondary or customary name and must be transliterated into Roman script; the transliterated name is the binding legal name registered. The name must include a corporate designator such as 'Limited' or 'Ltd' for a limited liability international company and must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing names on the national or international companies register.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name is valid for 30 days and may be renewed once for an additional 30 days upon application to the Registrar of Companies. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar within 14 days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds of distinctiveness and, where relevant, attaching a letter of consent from the holder of a conflicting name. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may administratively appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 21 days, and thereafter may seek judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa in accordance with the Companies Act 2001 and the International Companies Act 1987.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is not acceptable as the sole registered office. The International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the address of a licensed registered agent. A virtual office may be used only for administrative correspondence and business communications; the e-commerce retail of solar portable power products does not require a separate physical commercial premises in Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified at less than 5% company-site inspection risk per annum absent adverse risk indicators or abnormal transactional activity. The registered agent's office is subject to routine and impromptu inspections by the Registrar of Companies and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit; books and records must be produced within 24 hours of a lawful demand.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; ss. 4-9 (incorporation), s. 31 (registered office), ss. 38-48 (directors and secretary), s. 211 (exemptions from taxes and duties)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Charter Document)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued in any currency and denomination, with a nominal authorised capital commonly set at US$1 or US$1,000; no escrow or deposit account activation requirement prior to registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the First Board Resolution of the Company, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association, as executed by the subscribers, are adopted as the Company's governing charter. RESOLVED that the subscription of shares and the initial paid-up capital recorded in the Statement of Capital be ratified and accepted. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at the office of the Registered Agent in Apia, Samoa, and the Registered Agent be authorized to receive statutory notices. RESOLVED that [Director A] and [Director B] be appointed as the first Directors, and [Secretary] be appointed as the Company Secretary, each holding office in accordance with the Articles. RESOLVED that the Directors be authorized to open bank accounts and to integrate payment processing services for the Company's online retail operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa (online filing via SIFA e-Registry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two or three proposed corporate names for pre-approval in descending preference order. Ensure that each proposed name ends with 'International Company', 'IC', 'Ltd', 'Corp', or 'Inc.' and does not conflict with an existing registered name or a prohibited term under the International Companies Act 1987. The Registrar will issue a Name Reservation Certificate upon clearance.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Request Form (Form IC-NR)
Certificate of Incorporation of any corporate applicant, if applicable
Passport copy and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner
Banker's or legal practitioner's reference letter for the subscriber or director
Completed due diligence questionnaire under SIFA Anti-Money Laundering Rules 2017
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a fresh name request with alternative names, or appeal the Registrar's decision within 14 days by written submission under s. 7(4) of the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Charter Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed Registered Agent, Samoa International Finance Authority, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed Registered Agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, consistent with the Schedule to the International Companies Act 1987. Each subscriber must execute the charter document in the presence of a witness, with signatures notarized if the subscriber is a body corporate. The Registered Agent must sign the Consent to Act as Registered Agent and commit to maintaining the registered office at its licensed address.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association, executed by each subscriber and witnessed
Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent (Form IC-RA)
Consent to Act as Registered Agent signed by the licensed SIFA agent
Certified passport copies and proof of address for all subscribers
Notarized corporate resolutions and certificate of incumbency if a subscriber is a company
Client due diligence file (CDD records, source of funds declaration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify execution, witnessing, or notarization defects identified by the Registered Agent or Registrar, re-execute the charter, and resubmit with corrected subscriber particulars within 5 business days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed application with the executed Charter Document, Name Reservation Certificate, and prescribed government fees to the Registrar. The Registrar will examine the application for compliance with the Act, verify the absence of unlawful objects, and issue the Certificate of Incorporation upon satisfaction. Payment of the filing fee must be made by SWIFT transfer or bank draft in U.S. dollars.
required_dossiers: Completed Registration of an International Company Application (Form IC-1)
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association (two certified copies)
Certificate of Name Reservation issued in Step 1
Declaration of Compliance executed by each subscriber
Government filing fee remittance advice (SWIFT confirmation or bank draft)
Registered Agent's undertaking and licensed status certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond in writing to any SIFA query notice within 14 days, file an amended Form IC-1 or additional due diligence evidence, and re-submit for registration. If the Registrar rejects the application, file a formal appeal under s. 9 of the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Appointment of Directors and Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFA, and the Company's Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, file the Notice of Directors and Secretary with the Registrar. Ensure that at least one director is an individual, that the company secretary, if an individual, holds an appropriate licence, and that all consents to act are executed. The Registered Agent will then open the statutory registers (register of members, register of directors, register of charges) and prepare the common seal.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Notice of Directors and Secretary (Form IC-DS)
Consent to Act as Director signed by each director
Consent to Act as Secretary signed by the company secretary
Registered Agent's confirmation of statutory registers opened
Certified ID and address proof of each director and the secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notice of Directors is refused for defective signatures, correct the execution block, re-notarize if needed, and re-file; any late filings attract a fixed penalty fee which may be waived upon showing of reasonable cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exemption Confirmation and Banking Integration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) and commercial banks licensed by the Central Bank of Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Certificate of Good Standing and a written confirmation of tax exemption status for the International Company. Open a corporate bank account with a Samoan licensed commercial bank or a foreign correspondent bank, presenting the Charter Document, Certificate of Incorporation, resolution authorizing account opening, and economic substance declarations if requested. Thereafter, execute the Stripe and Affirm BNPL merchant agreements using the Company's corporate banking credentials.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing from SIFA
Extract from the Register of Directors and Register of Members
SIFA Tax Exemption Confirmation Letter
Board Resolution authorizing bank account opening and payment gateway engagement (Stripe / Affirm BNPL)
Passport copies, bank references, and police clearance certificates for directors as required by bank CDD
W-8BEN-E form (if applicable) for U.S.-connected payment flow
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide audited financials or a legal opinion from Samoan counsel; if tax exemption confirmation is delayed, seek an SIFA written ruling; alternatively, open the account with a second licensed bank or a fintech banking partner that accepts offshore ICs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Division of Trade and Industry, Apia, Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - ISIC 4791 direct online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels is a non-industrial e-commerce activity; no industrial operating license or manufacturing permit is mandated under Samoan law. An International Company is exempt from general business licensing, and no domestic trading license is required provided the retail sales are executed exclusively with non-resident customers.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA registration or full EIA Report required for pure online retail, administrative office, and repackaging-only activity; an EIA would be triggered only if the Company establishes physical industrial manufacturing, bulk battery storage exceeding threshold quantities, or land development works under Schedule 2 of the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial discharge regime for e-commerce operations; if a fulfillment and returns warehouse is established in Samoa, comply with the Waste Management (Sitting and Disposal) Rules 2020 for e-waste segregation, the Water Resources Management Act 2008 for no-contamination runoff, and the Ozone Layer Protection Regulations 2000 for any refrigerant-containing equipment. Used solar panels and lithium batteries must be handled through licensed e-waste recyclers and cannot be landfilled.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) for any commercial office, fulfillment center, or warehouse; structural and building load clearance under the Building Act 2016 for the premises; and an Occupational Safety and Health workplace clearance from the MCIL-OSH Division covering electrical safety, lithium battery handling procedures, fire extinguisher provision, and emergency evacuation planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Ministry for Revenue (Inland Revenue Department), Taxpayer Portal: https://www.majomali.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity engaging in taxable supplies in Samoa must apply for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAGST registration via the Ministry for Revenue's Online Taxpayer Services portal. Application requires constitutional documents, foreign registration certificate, and a Samoa-appointed local fiscal representative where no permanent establishment exists. The Ministry issues an eight-digit TIN within 5-10 business days after verification; the TIN integrates with Customs ASYCUDA World for import/export transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa International Companies are automatically treated as non-resident tax-exempt vehicles under the International Companies Act 1987 and the Income Tax Ordinance 2015, provided they carry on business outside Samoa. There is no check-the-box election. The company may elect by written notice to become a resident company subject to normal Samoan income tax if that status is advantageous for treaty access or bankability; hybrid mismatch elections are not available under Samoan domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 75,000 (annual taxable turnover threshold; non-resident e-commerce operators supplying digital and electronically supplied services are required to register regardless of threshold if sales to Samoan residents exceed WST 50,000 over a rolling 12-month period)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital e-invoicing APIs. Tax invoices may be issued in paper or electronic form, but must include a unique sequential tax invoice number, the seller's TIN, buyer's TIN (if a registered business), description, quantity, price, and VAGST wording. Businesses exporting goods must transmit export invoices and customs declarations through ASYCUDA World; no government digital stamping is required for export zero-rating. A phased e-invoicing mandate is under legislative review with pilot filing beginning in tax year 2026.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under the VAGST Act 1994 to tangible personal property exported by a registered supplier where ownership transfers to a non-resident customer, goods leave Samoa physically by carrier, and the supplier retains documentary proof that the goods have been consigned or delivered to an overseas destination. For online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels, the supply qualifies as a zero-rated export if the seller ships from a Samoan warehouse to a foreign customer's international address, the export declaration is made within 21 days, and the consideration is paid through an international financial channel. Services closely related to the exported goods (warranty, remote support) are zero-rated only when supplied to a non-resident and provided in connection with the exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form CED) via ASYCUDA World
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical dispatch from Samoa
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT confirmation evidencing receipt of payment from a non-resident buyer
Commercial tax invoice with zero-rated indication and supplier TIN
Digital proof of final delivery confirmation (signed TNT/FedEx/DHL POD or customs release delivered copy)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may conduct a retrospective audit within 7 years after the end of the export tax period. Where zero-rating is unsupported, the VAGST originally treated as zero-rated is immediately re-assessed as a taxable supply with 15% VAGST, plus a late payment penalty of 25% and interest at the statutory monthly rate from the originally due date. Fraudulent zero-rating claims (false export declarations, non-arrival of goods, or sham invoices) attract administrative penalties up to 150% of the avoided VAGST, and individual actors may face a criminal fine up to WST 200,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years under s.67 of the Tax Administration Act 2012. The Ministry maintains a published 'Export Zero-Rate Substantiation Checklist' which must be retained in the electronic tax records for a minimum period of 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), operating through its Exchange Control and Banking Supervision Departments under the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Exchange Control Regulations 1985 and the Financial Institutions Act 2008
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoa tala (WST) is a managed-float domestic currency that is not freely convertible outside Samoa. The legal framework distinguishes current-account payments, which are generally authorized for goods and services, from capital-account movements, which require CBS permission or a delegated authorization issued to commercial banks. Profit remittances from a Samoa International Company holding Samoan bank assets are permitted only with audited financial statements, a solvency certificate, evidence of beneficial ownership, and a tax clearance certificate where a resident tax liability exists. For an International Company operating exclusively with non-resident counterparties, CBS treats equity contributions, dealer-to-dealer transfers, and offshore settlement receipts as exempted exchange-control transactions provided no Samoan-resident person or Samoan-sourced activity is involved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa's Exchange Control Regulations require resident exporters to repatriate all export proceeds to Samoa within a prescribed period and, absent a specific foreign-currency account approval, to sell the foreign exchange to an authorized dealer in exchange for WST. The standard bank-level rule is credit to the exporter's Samoan bank account upon receipt and surrender to an authorized dealer within 30 days unless CBS has approved a Foreign Currency Account. A Samoa International Company engaged in direct online retail of portable power products is generally exempted from the resident surrender requirement when title to goods passes outside Samoa, payment is received into a non-resident settlement account, and no Samoan bank account is used for collection. If settlement is received into a Samoan bank account, CBS expects the IC to justify the credit by reference to its non-resident trade and may require the proceeds to be reconverted or transferred offshore.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_account_permission_thresholds: There are no published Samoan statutory monetary thresholds, but every authorized dealer in Samoa applies its own CBS-approved delegated limits for investment inflows and outward remittances. Transactions above approximately WST 100,000 equivalent, or any remittance whose stated purpose appears capital-related, normally require CBS Form EC-1 approval together with the IC certificate of incumbency, registered agent confirmation, board resolution, and proof of non-resident trade activity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. The Samoa International Company may open accounts at fully licensed local banks, but offshore digital EMI platforms without a Samoan banking licence have low viability because under the Financial Institutions Act 2008 only entities authorized by the CBS may deploy payment or depository services inside Samoa. An unlicensed EMI may still be used exclusively outside Samoa as a settlement account for customer card payments received through Stripe or Affirm BNPL, but such an EMI must not claim to transact in Samoa and must supply full evidence of its own AML/CFT licensing in a recognized FATF-compliant jurisdiction. For high transactional volume in USD or EUR, an EMI account embedded through an EEA-licensed bank is preferable, yet corresponding Samoan banks may reject inbound wires from non-bank payment service providers unless the EMI's licence and source-of-funds audit trail are documented.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: All Samoan authorized dealers require at least one director, beneficial owner, or designated authorized representative to appear in person, generally at the bank's head office in Apia, before account activation. Remote video onboarding is not standardized for International Companies, and a new IC is highly unlikely to be opened without an in-person KYC interview or the physical attendance of a locally licensed registered agent holding an explicit board-approved mandate. For the IC, every bank will require a notarized copy of the International Company certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency, memorandum and articles, the registered agent acceptance letter, full passport and proof of residence for all directors and ultimate beneficial owners, and a certified banking resolution authorizing signatories. The stricter stance arises from Samoa's former IMF/FATF mutual evaluation concerns and the corresponding banks' insistence on physical meeting records for tax-exempt offshore structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company controlled by a non-resident mixed-nationality beneficial-ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete direct and indirect ownership chart; notarized passports and proof of address for all natural persons owning more than 10%; source of wealth declarations for each beneficial owner; certified trust deed and trustee resolution if a family trust is involved; written confirmation from the Samoan registered agent that the IC maintains no resident business or Samoan real property; and a board resolution designating the purpose of the Samoan bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High projected card settlement velocity from Stripe and Affirm BNPL inconsistent with a small Samoa office
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply executed merchant service agreements, platform risk-control summaries, settlement schedules, expected monthly volume, product catalog pages, underlying supplier contracts, logistics agreements with third-party warehouses, sample commercial invoices, consumer cancellation and refund policies, and an independent legal opinion confirming that all merchants are non-resident consumers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually large inbound equity funding from a related offshore entity or family trust
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide original share subscription agreement, funds-transfer instruction from the remitting institution, confirmed source of funds in the remitter's own account for at least three months, a cash-flow business plan, board minutes approving the capital injection, and a written representation that the funds are not the proceeds of any unlawful activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to Chinese solar-panel manufacturers and Taiwan battery suppliers may appear as a typical procurement mismatch when the business is physically in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a group-wide e-commerce operational manual showing that Samoa is the parent merchant of record while procurement and fulfillment are performed by contract manufacturers; provide purchase orders, inspection certificates, bill of lading, customs declaration forms, freight invoices, and counterparty KYC files; and preserve every supplier invoice reconcilable with each customer purchase record.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection from a non-resident shareholder or affiliated group should be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the remitting jurisdiction to the Samoan authorized dealer, with the beneficiary name matching the International Company exactly, the beneficial owner's shareholder name included in the originator field, and a purpose code identifying direct investment equity injection (generally exchange-control purpose code for 'equity capital for non-financial enterprise' or 'foreign direct investment capital' under the CBS reporting taxonomy). The remitting bank must be in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction and must provide full correspondent-bank details; the Samoan receiving bank will require the IC's registered agent to submit a CBS declaration on the exchange control form, a board resolution approving the equity subscription, and a legal-capital calculation from the corporate service provider. Funds received for the sole purpose of share capital should be credited to a clearly marked capital escrow account and then moved to the operational account only after the on-boarded banker has completed conversion of the remittance into WST or retention in USD under an approved Foreign Currency Account arrangement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for inventory purchases, freight forwarding, fulfillment-center fees, and customer duty advances are executed through SWIFT MT103 if telegraphic transfer is used, with purpose code '121 – payments for imports of goods' or 'goods not elsewhere classified' as mapped by the CBS. For large, periodic supplier settlements, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the Samoan bank is accepted if the underlying trade documents are clean; UCP600 must govern all documentary terms. When the IC settles on the same day to suppliers in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, or Singapore, the bank wires through its USD nostro network using an MT202 cover instruction; the Samoan bank will debit the USD account directly, avoiding WST conversion, if the account is a Foreign Currency Account. The IC must keep full invoice-level documentation to support each outward payment and must never combine personal expenses with supplier remittances.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts with the Samoan authorized dealer on a covered commercial invoice basis
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/WST or USD/CNY for rolling inventory exposure, provided the underlying open foreign-currency exposure is evidenced by supplier invoices
Cross-currency swaps between USD, AUD, EUR, and WST entered solely to match the duration of commercial receivables and supplier payables
Spot foreign exchange transactions executed through the CBS-authorized dealer under the IC's approval status
Vanilla bank deposit or zero-cost collar transactions if approved in writing by CBS and the Samoan bank's credit committee for economically hedging only the net open position
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.cbs_filing_and_audit_coordination: The International Company will be required to coordinate all bank statements, ECB filings, and treasury documentation with its Samoan registered agent and external auditor. CBS and tax authorities may require annual declarations demonstrating that the account movement is consistent with non-resident online retail. All forward contracts and swaps, even where immaterial, must be shadowed by external valuation reports and presented with the audited financial statements to preserve the tax-exempt status and avoid the company being treated as carrying on a financial institution business in Samoa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company License Fee and Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of USD 100 per month or portion thereof; continued non-payment and non-filing for six consecutive months exposes the company to administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registrar after prior notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Agent and Registered Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual license fee due date; no separate statutory extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent and registered office in Samoa constitutes a continuing contravention of the International Companies Act, punishable by fine and enabling the Registrar to strike the company off the Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the incorporation anniversary; immediate update required upon any shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalty for non-compliance; reliance on inaccurate UBO information may be treated as a regulatory offence and is considered in SIFA enforcement proceedings, including possible suspension of the company's licensed status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent statutory audit is required for a Samoa International Company not carrying on business in Samoa, provided the company files the prescribed exemption declaration with SIFA. An audit becomes mandatory if the company is registered as a foreign-owned financial institution, holds a specific license requiring audited financial statements, or otherwise fails the annual exemption declaration process.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; directors may adopt simple cash-basis internal accounts for exempt offshore non-licensee companies where no auditor is appointed

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must maintain a current beneficial ownership register reflecting the ultimate beneficial owner, whether a person or legal entity. On any shareholding transfer, directors must deliver an updated UBO notification to the registered agent within 14 days; the transfer is not effective against SIFA until the record is updated, and the annual confirmation must restate all UBO data as of the anniversary date.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a validly registered Samoa International Company; 27% for ordinary Samoa resident companies if the exempt status is lost or revoked.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Zero-rate international company exemption under the Samoa International Companies Act 2012; no Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, or stamp duty on offshore business; annual fixed government levy regime; exemption is conditional on no Samoan-source business activities and compliance with the International Company filing obligations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Samoan corporate income tax return is issued for an exempt International Company. The recurring filing is the International Company Annual Return / Annual Government Levy declaration submitted by the licensed Samoa registered agent to the Samoa International Companies Registry through the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) registry portal. If exemption is lost, the ordinary Company Income Tax Return is filed through Samoa's Ministry of Revenue e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and government levy are due in the registry renewal cycle based on the anniversary month of incorporation; no annual CIT return deadline applies while the IC exemption is maintained. A defaulting IC is struck off if the annual declaration remains unfiled after prescribed reminders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, registration number, date of incorporation, authorized capital and issued share capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident founders do not file directly; the registered agent transcribes the exact Certificate of Incorporation data and confirms all capital entries are in the approved currency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B - Samoa Addresses and Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office in Samoa, registered agent name and licence number, and offshore correspondence details if any.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A physical Samoan registered office is mandatory; a PO Box alone is insufficient. The registered agent must be named and charged with accepting service of process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, addresses, nationality, director/beneficial owner details, and share allocation percentages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors should provide passport copies, proof of address, and UBO declarations; this information is held by the registered agent for FIU AML/KYC inspection, not filed on the public register where exemptions apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the International Company has not carried on business in Samoa, has no fixed local establishment, has no Samoan-resident customers, and has not derived Samoan-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Online retail of solar portable power systems to non-resident buyers via Stripe or Affirm is compatible with this declaration, provided no inventory, employees, marketing office, or delivery hubs are located in Samoa and no sales are made to Samoa residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part E - Solvency and Compliance Attestation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of solvency, confirmation of continued compliance with the International Companies Act 2012, and registered agent certification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident director or, in practice, the registered agent signs the attestation; a non-resident director who knowingly signs a false local-business declaration triggers director liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return/levy triggers registry late charges and, on continued default, automatic strike-off and dissolution, reinstatement fees, and potential personal liability of directors for government fees owed before restoration. Because the exempt IC has no CIT return obligation, ordinary CIT late-filing daily surcharges do not apply to the exempt entity.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% withholding tax on dividends declared by a validly tax-exempt Samoa International Company; distributions are treated as outside the Samoan tax net. If the entity were a taxable ordinary resident company, the non-resident dividend WHT rate is 15% final withholding under Samoa's Income Tax Act.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: In the normal course, no DTA claim is required because the International Company's profits and distributions are already exempt in Samoa. If a withholding obligation arises after revocation of exemption, the non-resident payee must submit a Samoa Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by Samoa's Ministry of Revenue, complete the relevant treaty claim form through the paying agent, and supply a beneficial-ownership declaration before payment. Treaty relief is optional and must be invoked in writing; failure to provide the TRC and ownership statement before the WHT due date causes the domestic 15% rate to be applied in full.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoa non-resident withholding tax on Samoan-source interest and royalties is 15%. Treaties may reduce the rate to 0-10% for beneficial owners, subject to TRC and limitation-on-benefits verification. Interest and royalties paid by an exempt International Company to non-residents for foreign IP or offshore financing are not Samoan-source and incur no Samoan WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Samoa Local File or Master File threshold applies to a tax-exempt International Company. For a taxable Samoa resident company, transfer pricing documentation is not triggered by a bright-line WST monetary threshold; rather, all cross-border related-party transactions are subject to audit under the arm's-length standard, and documentary evidence must be contemporaneous once the value exceeds de minimis or defensive-documentation expectations. A consolidated group with Samoan operations and EUR 750 million or more global revenue may also be required to file Country-by-Country reporting, expressed by Samoa in WST equivalent at the applicable central-bank rate.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not maintain Caribbean- or Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations. Nevertheless, an International Company must have real and demonstrable offshore substance: a licensed registered agent, registered office, board records, bank account and decision-making outside Samoa, plus foreign-source income. A company operating as a bare conduit or shell for the purpose of routing e-commerce profits may be recharacterized under Samoa's general anti-avoidance principles and by the beneficial owner's home-country CFC, controlled-foreign-company, or economic-substance rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized Local Business / Loss of International Company Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling to Samoa residents, maintaining a Samoan warehouse, using Samoan couriers/delivery hubs, hiring Samoan staff, or otherwise carrying on business in Samoa while continuing to claim the tax-exempt International Company status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation or deemed loss of IC exemption; taxation of the entire income at the 27% corporate rate; back-tax and interest; registry strike-off; monetary penalties under the International Companies Act 2012 and Income Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly misstate the offshore declaration are jointly liable for the unpaid tax, penalties and registry fees; the corporate veil is pierced for false declaration, and directors face disqualification, civil restitution, travel bans and imprisonment if the conduct amounts to tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely reporting that sales are exclusively to foreign buyers when in fact sales are made to Samoa residents; understating income or hiding locally-sourced gross sales via Stripe/Affirm settlement routing to foreign accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of income at the standard rate, civil penalties of up to 150% of the tax shortfall, statutory interest, criminal fines, and imprisonment for willful tax evasion under Samoa's Revenue Administration legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs or causes a false return/declaration can be personally assessed, ordered to make civil restitution of the evaded tax, banned from leaving Samoa, and imprisoned; the company's separate legal personality is disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa IC as an invoice or payment intermediary without genuine board meetings, contracts, inventory risk, cash-flow authority, local books or foreign bank operations; or structuring the company to avoid the shareholder's home-country tax and reporting obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoan anti-avoidance doctrine the entity may be treated as a resident, transparent or sham vehicle, with all income recharacterized in the hands of the beneficial owner; foreign tax authorities may impose CFC, economic-substance or GAAR penalties; the IC may be struck off for failure to demonstrate existence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Participation in a sham causes directors to be liable for fraudulent misrepresentation and for debts of the company; courts may impose restitution, asset tracing orders, travel bans, director disqualification and imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting payments from sanctioned or high-risk counterparties, allowing Stripe/Affirm funds to be commingled with client funds, failing to provide beneficial-owner information to the registered agent, or conducting transactions for third parties without an economic rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and administrative penalties imposed by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, freezing of bank accounts, forfeiture of the digital-payment proceeds, suspension or revocation of the registered agent's licence, and criminal prosecution for money laundering and terrorist financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly involved in laundering proceeds or evading AML controls are personally subject to criminal fines, confiscation of property, travel bans, and imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced for money laundering and fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling solar portable products to a related foreign distributor at non-arm's-length prices to erode Samoa profit; paying excessive royalties, management fees or interest to a related offshore IP-holding entity; issuing invoices for services that are not actually performed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority transfer-pricing adjustments to gross profit/expenses, additional tax at 27%, penalty of up to 150% of the undercharged tax, statutory interest, and, in fraud cases, criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs false intercompany agreements or knowingly causes the mispricing can be held jointly and severally liable for the adjustment, restitution and penalties; courts may impose travel restrictions and imprisonment in aggravated fraud cases.
